newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower on generation unit returns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower on generation unit returns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Wednesday as idled generation units returned to service and seasonable weather gripped the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"A lot of generation is coming back, the daily (physical power) markets are off, and a lot of utilities are sellers now," said on Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1220 EDT, NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) was trading down $1.06 at the day's low of $26.60 following exchanges as high as $27.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), while August PV was down 38 cents at $29.60 per MWh following trades in a range of $29.40-29.75 per MWh.

July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 61 cents at $17.00 after exchanges in the $16.60-17.10 range, while August was down 42 cents at the day's high of $20.80 following trade as low as $20.50 per MWh.
As of 1130 EDT, NYMEX said an estimated total of 248 COB and 167 PV contracts had traded.
Sources said prices for next-day power in the West continued to fall, with peak PV power assessed at $24.00 from $29.00-31.00 on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery.
Two nuclear power units in the U.S. West, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3, were in the process of returning to full output following outages.
Arizona Public Service said Tuesday Palo Verde 3 would hold at 35 percent power for a few days and ramp up to full output Friday.
Diablo Canyon 1 was at 30 percent output Wednesday morning, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was ramping up power and was operating at 670 MW of capacity as of Wednesday morning.
A 550 MW unit at the Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming will shut Wednesday and stay down until Sunday for planned maintenance, industry sources said.
Also, Bonneville Power Administration dropped its peak power price offers by $2.00 for Thursday delivery to $14.00 per MWh at COB.
As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas futures were trading up 4.7 cents at $2.145 per million British thermal units.

Temperatures in the West were called to average near to slightly above normal into early next week with above normal precipitation in the eastern sections of the Northwest and northern areas of the Southwest.
